yarn.meaning: Every beat survives: the date muddle and the flume, "he'd swap sides himself", the fight list, the straddle-bug "all the way to Mexico", the parson's wife and "'Well, I'll risk two-and-a-half she don't, anyway.'", the mare fetching up "about a neck in front". Additions like "Talk about a one-track mind, ay." and "Never pretty, but she got there." only react to what is there.
yarn.sense: Terms fit: "lobbed into the camp", "cashed up or stony broke" for flush/busted, "Chook fight", "properly crook", "takin' the piss" for 'only in fun'. "on the frog and toad" for a bug's road is a stretch, and "a dead-set legend" overstates 'a good man'.
yarn.authenticity: Mostly a real voice: "happy as", "a lucky bugger, I'll tell ya", "Whips of the young fellas", "slow as". A couple of stock pieces ("on the frog and toad", "Strewth,") read a bit bolted on.
yarn.register: A full level-5 yarn with "bugger", "bloody", "flamin'" and "takin' the piss": inside vulgarity 2 and at the weight asked.
yarn.tone: Keeps the deadpan rambling narrator; the punchline "'Well, I'll risk two-and-a-half she don't, anyway.'" lands as dry as the original.
yarn.flow: Reads aloud easily; asides such as "-- well, wherever the little bugger was goin' --" mimic the narrator's drift without pile-ups.
yarn.variety: Varied: "cashed up", "stony broke", "lobbed", "dosh", "Whips of", "crook". "bugger" comes three times and "bet ya" repeats, but nothing dominates.
yarn.essence: Unmistakably the Jim Smiley yarn: keeps "curiousest bloke", "foller that straddle-bug", "Dangedest feller" and the "m-o-r-e dust" spelling.

engine.meaning: Most of the original is kept word for word, but edits break sense: "the bloody big flume stoushn't finished" garbles 'warn't finished', "anythin' that lobed" garbles 'turned up', "before he reckoned" changes 'before he thought', "for a beaut while" changes 'for a good while'.
engine.sense: Several terms take the wrong sense: "stoushn't" (a stoush is a fight), "lobed" for 'turned up', "for a beaut while" (beaut = excellent) for a long sickness, "before he reckoned", "she get rapt'n desperate" (rapt = delighted) for 'excited'.
engine.authenticity: Stage-Australian: interjections bolted onto sentence starts ("Far out, Rev. Leonidas W.", "Fair dinkum, any way", "Crikey, he was", "Bloody hell, whips of of") and a closing "Stone the flamin' crows." US dialect ("warn't", "ary side", 'Thish-yer') is left in alongside.
engine.register: Level 5 asked, but the body is largely untranslated ("there couldn't be no solit'ry thing mentioned but that feller'd offer to bet on it, and take ary side ya please"), with slang sprinkled on. Swearing ("bloody", "bugger") is within limits.
engine.tone: The deadpan survives where the original is untouched, but inserts like "Crikey," and "Stone the flamin' crows." tip it toward pantomime.
engine.flow: Broken joins: "Mind ya, H'm, Reverend Le--well", "whips of of the young fellas", "Anyway, why, it never made no difference", "dust'n raising".
engine.variety: Leans on bolted-on openers ("Far out", "Fair dinkum", "Crikey", "Bloody hell", "Anyway") and "ya" substitutions throughout.
engine.essence: Recognisably the original because most of it is the original verbatim, but inserts such as "a beaut while" and "cobber" muddy it.

unharnessed.meaning: All points kept: the date muddle and flume, "he'd just swap sides", the fight list, the straddle-bug to Mexico, the parson's wife and "'Well, I'll put two and a half on her not making it, anyway.'", and the mare "about a neck in front".
unharnessed.sense: Terms fit: "rocked up at the camp", "have a punt on it", "rolling in it or flat stony broke", "taking the piss" for 'only in fun', "arse end of the race". "lucky as all get-out" is right in sense but American.
unharnessed.authenticity: Sounds like a real Australian: "happy as Larry", "the mad bastard", "Chook fight", "crook, real crook". "lucky as all get-out" is a US idiom and "flinging her legs about all floppy" is flat.
unharnessed.register: A full level-5 retelling with "bloody", "bastard", "sod", "taking the piss", "arse end": inside vulgarity 2.
unharnessed.tone: Deadpan narrator intact; the bet against the parson's wife lands flat and funny.
unharnessed.flow: Smooth throughout, though "bloody" stacks up near the end ("some bloody thing", "every bloody time").
unharnessed.variety: Good spread ("rocked up", "punt", "rolling in it", "pipes up", "happy as Larry") but "bloody" is used five times and "bastard" twice.
unharnessed.essence: Clearly the Smiley yarn, but the dialect flavour is smoothed out: "follow" for 'foller', 'Thish-yer' and 'dangdest' gone, "galloping and sprawling up" for 'cavorting and straddling up'.

yarn.original: how long he was on the road
yarn.why: Rhyming slang reads as a stock tourist touch here.

yarn.quote: a dead-set legend and a top bloke with it
yarn.why: Inflates a plain 'good man' into gushing praise, louder than the deadpan original.

yarn.quote: Talk about a one-track mind, ay.
yarn.why: Added tag explains a joke the original leaves deadpan.

engine.quote: the bloody big flume stoushn't finished
engine.why: Nonsense word made by swapping 'stoush' into 'warn't'; the sentence no longer parses.
Misspelt and misapplied 'lobbed'; reads as a typo.
'Beaut' means excellent; wrong sense for a long illness.

engine.original: she get excited and desperate like

engine.why: 'Reckoned' means supposed; 'before he thought' is lost.

Far out, Rev. Leonidas W. Mind ya, H'm
engine.why: Stock interjections stuck onto the opening break the narrator's hesitation.
US dialect left untranslated across most of the text; slang is only sprinkled on.
Stock pastiche tag added at the end.

unharnessed.why: US idiom in an Aussie voice.

unharnessed.quote: every bloody time she'd pull up at the stand
unharnessed.original: always fetch up at the stand
unharnessed.why: 'Bloody' is leaned on through the closing stretch.

unharnessed.quote: come galloping and sprawling up, flinging her legs about all floppy
unharnessed.original: come cavorting and straddling up, and scattering her legs around limber
unharnessed.why: Loses the vividness of 'cavorting' and 'limber'; 'all floppy' is flat.

summaries.yarn: A natural, full-strength Aussie yarn that keeps every beat and the deadpan; only a couple of stock touches.
summaries.engine: Largely the original with slang words swapped in, several in the wrong sense, plus broken grammar and stock interjections; well short of a level-5 retelling.
summaries.unharnessed: Natural, faithful full-strength retelling; a little flatter than the original's dialect and leans on 'bloody'.
